standard_prerequisites: An axiomatizable theory T extending Q with a derivability predicate satisfying the Hilbert-Bernays-Lob conditions P1 to P3: from a derivation of A one obtains a derivation of the provability of A; from a derivation of the provability of A-implies-B one obtains a derivation of the provability of A implies the provability of B; and from a derivation of A one obtains a derivation of the provability of the provability of A.
The fixed-point lemma for Q, used to obtain a sentence D equivalent in T to the provability of D implies A.
core_obligations: Given T derives the provability of A implies A, construct the fixed point D of the formula provability-of-y implies A.

Derive the twelve-step chain from the fixed-point equivalence to A: unpack the fixed point, apply condition P1 to the biconditional, apply P2 twice to push the box through the implication, apply P3 to the derivability of D, combine with the hypothesis to obtain the provability of D implies A, and close with the biconditional to reach D and then A.
proof_roadmap: Fix the fixed point D of the formula provability-of-y implies A and write the chain as a numbered derivation, each line justified by the previous lines plus exactly one derivability condition.

The key middle steps: P1 turns the derivation of the fixed-point equivalence into the provability of that implication; P2 applied twice extracts the provability of D implies the provability of the provability of D; P3 applied to the derivation of D obtained inside the chain yields the provability of D; the pieces compose to A.
difficulty_reason: A twelve-step formal chain in the derivability conditions where the self-referential fixed point is applied twice; the care points are the two condition-P2 pushes and the order in which the box is stripped.
